rule: WHEN a button is "pressed" -> DO squeeze about its centre to 0.76-0.80 (11-13 f down, ~19 f up at 60 fps) with a lighter fill (#4C4DF5 -> #7FA7F5); no overshoot, no ripple BECAUSE a clean squeeze reads as a deliberate tap. Add a hard cursor swap (arrow -> hand) 0.17 s before the click and shrink the hand to ~0.52 on the press. (M922, M928)
scope_note: Cursor grammars differ: PR-A09 keeps one cursor shape; PR-B11 permits arrow-to-hand. Keep the chosen source grammar; these are not universal live-product rules.

rule: WHEN there is no pointer, give the eye a carrier: a shaded 0.04 W bead riding the device rim during the camera move, growing x1.5-2.2 per 3 f into the next scene BECAUSE it directs attention and gives the next scene a literal origin. (M922)

WHEN a control moves numbers -> DO ease-in-out every counter off one handle (expo-out zoom 1.69 -> 1.00 in 48 f; counters 69 -> 100% / $60 -> $193 in 50 f, update every frame, no overshoot) BECAUSE the viewer reads cause and effect without text. (M923)

WHEN morphing UI between two layouts -> DO only narrow/clip (slider pill width 0.53 -> 0.005 W in 36 f, constant height, handle clipped by the edge, ticks dying one by one) and grow the new layout around the caret as staggered fades with 3-5 px de-blur + 18-20 px upward settle, group onsets ~0.1 s apart BECAUSE clipping reads as physical, staggers keep the eye ordered. (M923)

WHEN something is typed -> DO match the data: 28-30 chars/s with irregular 1-f holds for human prompts (M928), right-aligned growth around a fixed caret for fields (M923), per-glyph colour sweeps (dim -> white) at 4 f then 2 f cadence for system text (M921); never blink a caret BECAUSE the cadence tells who is typing. (M921, M923, M927, M928)
scope_note: This source keeps the caret solid; catalogue recipes may blink after completion. These are source-specific film grammars.

rule: WHEN using perspective -> DO use true perspective (track with horizon dropping as camera drops, label lying in the track plane, translucent hero object with blurred through-copy of the label), and give the hero a rise -> recede -> rush path with accelerating growth (5x faster in the last third), pinning its top edge BECAUSE it creates travel, not a scale-up. (M924)

WHEN the finale is a counter or a ring -> DO decelerate (3.1 pts/f -> 0.5 pts/f), park on 99 for 5 f, land 100 without a flash, and keep scaling the whole card (0.43 -> 0.89 W) through to the last frame BECAUSE the last 1% becomes suspense and the card feels like it keeps coming at you. (M924)

WHEN a question must turn into a brand -> DO make the brand mark the same object as the question's pointer: shapes collapse (cards round 3 -> 19% and shrink) into the mark, one 1-frame oversize pop at ~3x settled size (hard step 1.27, pop 1.30, settle by 1.67), mark slides left to lead the question, the question enters whole from the right (50% of travel in 2 f), then TWO independent soft masks erase the question and reveal the name in place (mint 25-45 px leading edge, erase front leading the reveal front, ~0.1 s gap) while the mark slides back right over the text as the name's tail BECAUSE the viewer's own answer is spent as the reveal, and nothing crossfades. (M926)

WHEN you build a CTA -> DO sequence tagline (1.7 s) -> second phrase (1.5 s) -> icon (0.8 s) -> wordmark, three hard cuts, the last into a dark ground; the icon only shrinks (accelerating 1.0 -> 0.70), the wordmark crashes from 3.75x with 96 stacked scaled copies as radial streaks (39% of the collapse in 1 f, 1.0x at 0.67 s) and keeps contracting with a slight flicker, accelerating again in the last 0.2 s, no fade, visible on the last frame; wordmark ink 0.28 W so empty space carries the glow BECAUSE the sign-off feels thrown at the viewer, then lingering. (M929)

WHEN showing 4 data surfaces in 4 s -> DO use one repeatable birth (1-frame slab, 25-30 px smear, grows to 0.5 H over ~0.47 s while darkening), ~0.75 s apart, one live micro-proof each (gauge to 77% of the arc, last digit rolls, waveform wipe), stack the previous card to a rear peek (left edge 0.50, 0.21 W) BECAUSE the repeat becomes a rhythm, the micro-proof proves it's live. (M927)

WHEN a state change happens to text -> DO use travelling soft-edged masks, not crossfades (M926 swap, M927 Limit row fades in as separate row while both rise 0.075 H) BECAUSE motion shows where it comes from.

WHEN one accent colour exists -> DO spend it on arrival flashes that decay to ink (ticker violet sweep -> white, "data" green -> ink, "making" mint 4-6 f -> white) and on one action (Close button) BECAUSE colour then marks the newest thing.

rule: WHEN you need the ground to change mid-scene -> DO ramp it as one continuous straight-sRGB track over 0.5-0.7 s timed to what is leaving (cards -> teal, #ECEEEB -> #41977F) BECAUSE a cut/fade of the ground breaks the continuity of the objects.
evidence_note: Source row has no per-row moment IDs; unverified, not a measured guarantee.

rule: WHEN a UI event is the point (switch, drop, click) → DO make the cause land first and the effect 1-2 frames after contact begins, flipping state in 2 frames (knob, one pale frame, full colour) with NO glow/ring; follow with the secondary cascade 5 frames later. BECAUSE the eye reads causality from the tiny gap and the sparse cleanliness lets the cascade carry the drama. (evidence: M933 master at 1.17-1.21 then rows from 1.42; M931 drop at 0.67)

WHEN one action propagates to a list ("authorize once, everyone") → DO a top-to-bottom cascade at 2-3 frames/item (0.08-0.12 s), 5-7 items, whole wave ≤0.6 s, uneven gaps (3,2,2,2,2,2) never uniform timer-looking. BECAUSE a wave short enough to hold in working memory reads as one gesture; too slow reads as a loading list. (M933, M935 gaps 3,3,2,2,2,4)

WHEN a wave crosses a 2D grid → DO origin-first, a convex front (centre rows lead outer rows by 3-6 f), ~5 f/column, items change on a 12 fps pose clock while the camera stays at 24-25 fps; orthogonal lattice with 5-10px jitter, never hex/random. BECAUSE the viewer sees "spreading" as geometry, and hand-posed items vs smooth camera gives craft without noise. (M934 WAVE table)

WHEN the camera whips between regions → DO 3-5 frames of travel: ease-in over ~10 frames (27% of travel), then 45-50% of travel in the 4 frames around the peak (~13% W per frame), then a 15-frame tail; add blur only if the film's language has blur (film A, C), otherwise change the content within the whip (panel/logo/lines exit with the pan). (M934, M931, M936)

WHEN you need an actual hard whip with a camera change → DO ramp blur+smear on the last 3 frames of the old view (text 8-20px, ~100px smear), cut with a one-frame discontinuity into a view that is ALREADY blurred (button as a smeared pill) and resolve over ~8 frames; swap scale at the cut (2x). BECAUSE both sides share blur so the cut is hidden and the arrival reads as inertia. (M931 1.53; M937 18px>80px)

WHEN you move a big card/panel as a "camera settle" → DO slow-in/fast-middle/long-tail: 27% of travel in the first 0.46 s, 42% in 3 frames, 25% in a 0.7 s tail, scale 1>0.6 simultaneously, no overshoot, never fully off screen (leave 0.20 W of its edge as an anchor). (M933 2.33-3.58)

WHEN highlighting a key word in a line → DO choose by metaphor: product-mechanic = hard-cut selection boxes (#354BAA solid, 4-5 frames each, one empty frame between boxes, text dims not inverts, one box per word, cut in AND out) fired the moment the line is complete; editorial = hand-drawn loop (5px stroke, 9 held 2-frame poses over 0.75 s, drawn from under an object, held ~0.7 s, exits as a NEW curl, still visible at the cut). Never both, never an underline/glow. BECAUSE the highlight must say which word is the claim without becoming an extra object. (M930, M933)

WHEN a hero number counts → DO one value per frame, with non-round steps (+8-9 each, 7 frames), the number growing 0.12>0.22 H while colour/blur resolve (grey, 5px blur > #5C sharp > black one beat after landing); hold solid 1.24 s; then fade its label up from blur 0.2 s after it lands. For 1..N counters: 1 frame (40 ms) per digit, growing ~12%/frame, last digit reaches size one beat later. BECAUSE a count that ends sharp in <0.3 s feels like impact; holds make it a fact. (M936)

WHEN comparing two quantities (30:00 vs 6 weeks) → DO render them at the same height (0.22 H), keep the sentence text small (0.067-0.08 H), reserve pure black for the figure and charcoal elsewhere, and never settle the second one (cropped at the edge mid-slide: 6 accelerates out -11,-12,-19,-30 px/f while "weeks" decelerates in -70,-62,-54). BECAUSE equal weight reads as a fair comparison; motion at the cut implies there is more. (M936)

WHEN removing/replacing words in a sequence → DO exit 1 frame apart (3-4 frames each, up 0.07 H + fade) and enter 2-5 frames apart from different offsets (0.07-0.22 H below) onto one baseline with exponential ease-out ~15 f; on the same pass overlap the exit with the next entrance by ~2 frames. BECAUSE exits are faster than entrances; overlap keeps reading momentum. (M938 0.00/0.12/0.20/0.32 in, 1.00/1.04/1.08/1.12 out)

WHEN a phrase needs word-by-word reading → DO whole words not letters: pop in 1 frame (or from 5px blur resolving in 4 f), offset right, each decelerating left on its own track (largest first step ~33px/f), colour ramping dark>grey for later words or grey>black in 4 stepped opacities (30/50/75/100), cadence 3-5 frames (accelerating 5,5,3,3), fixed slots, no re-centring. Typing only for UI text, left-anchored, 3-4 letters first. BECAUSE letter-typing makes titles look like a terminal; word-pops give rhythm that matches speech. (M936, M934, M937 "understand")

WHEN a logo grid appears → DO start oversized (2.5x, tiles are giant cropped squares), pull back in two surges (2.5>1.85 in 0.28 s, near-stall 0.28 s, >1.08 in 0.32 s, >0.875), tiles appear as outline glyph 1 frame apart (4 logos in 4 frames) then flip to filled in single frames in an uneven order (2,2,1 f), a late logo enters already filled from an edge as the pull-back reveals its cell, and pale filler cells pop (no fade) to make a lattice. The title sits in a 2x1 hole in the grid. BECAUSE the pull-back is the counting device: scale change gives a reveal rhythm with no extra elements. (M937)

WHEN the opening word is the thesis → DO make it enormous (0.91 W ink, 0.33 H), slow shrink 18% in 0.6 s, then accelerate (0.74>0.25 in 0.48 s) while blur ramps 0>18px and opacity 1>0.42, and hard-cut (no white frame) into the next defocused state. BECAUSE the viewer registers a thesis word before it leaves; the collapse is the transition. (M937)

WHEN an entry is a "reveal of identity" (hero title) → DO per-glyph blur-streak entrance (10>1px in 8 frames, ~1 glyph/frame, cold-blue>white in 0.3 s), a multi-phase path (glide, lift with 1-frame smear, jump with smear) to rest, additive glow dying by 0.5 s, and let the other words arrive by different mechanics (whole-word slide vs scattered glyph fragments). BECAUSE variety inside one line avoids the "typewriter title" look. (M930)

WHEN a title becomes a product shot → DO open a gap: insert a 0.03 thumbnail at the gap (wide 0.09x0.07), spread words (RGB split up to 9px, scale 0.06>0.09), HARD-CUT the title in 1 frame on the same frame the card box accelerates (35px of height/frame), and let a cover-fit video crop from wide to portrait (never stretched, always playing). BECAUSE the cut-on-motion makes the swap invisible. (M930)

WHEN dragging a card into a field → DO give the target a reaction stack: grow target 0.08 H, hover rim (#73C8F2) 0.4 s early, tilt card -8° at crest then 0° at drop, 2-frame crest hold, then ONE frame to attachment + cursor swap + flash, + a 0.2 s residual wash sliding off. Ground tint shifts 4% during the drag. BECAUSE one-frame snap with stacked feedback feels physical. (M931)

WHEN a cursor performs a click → DO: long decel in (first step 79px/f), hover 3-8 frames, swap art for press in 1 frame (or depress 0.03 H), recoil 0.92 over 3-5 frames, never ring/ripple on the cursor; put the click response in the UI (tint plate 0.25 opacity, button 0.81, no rebound); end the film ON the maximum compression. Pose changes (pointing>thumbs-up) are 1-frame swaps with an 8px bounce, no scale. BECAUSE cursor choreography is the product demo; hold-then-swap gives anticipation. (M930, M931, M933, M935)

WHEN you reveal a menu/popup → DO height-wipe (0.29>0.41 H in 4 frames) with rows fading in at 1-2 frame stagger, divider growing L>R, hover square behind the trigger appearing 0.17 s BEFORE the hand lands, popup 6 frames after landing; exit slides down while riding the zoom and fades only in the last 4 frames. BECAUSE staged reveal avoids a whole-panel fade. (M935)

WHEN many tokens must become instances → DO match-cut layout across clips (same lattice positions), let identical tokens morph into varied content at staggered 0.04-0.12 s offsets (inner pair first, outer last), with greeting text typed on, while the centre dot grows 0.01>0.9 W to become the next stage, contents on a separate scale track. BECAUSE continuity of position carries the eye through a hard cut. (M934>M935)

WHEN you stagger exits of physical objects → DO simulate bodies individually (own path, rotation, bounce 0.03 H, slight rotation overshoot -95>-90), settle by 1.8-2.2 s then HOLD 0.8-1.0 s motionless as the "weight" beat, then let the wash arrive; use ≥ one extra body entering late (0.60) to avoid choreographed uniformity. BECAUSE a group translation reads as a slide, individual bodies read as consequence. (M938)

WHEN washing a scene into a brand → DO a 0.28 H-feathered colour haze from the bottom (0.4 s rise), swell content 1.07>1.20x as it peaks, fade the objects bottom-first, then at the peak frame change to a pale gradient (never solid colour), build the mark bar by bar (1 per frame, gradient bars darkest-first right>left), the wordmark 1 glyph/frame with 5-frame grey>black fades and tracking collapsing +20>-3px while sliding left 0.11 W; keep shrinking the lockup (1>0.835 in 0.8 s, accelerating). BECAUSE the brand arrives as a resolution, and a shrinking lockup never feels pasted. (M938)

WHEN a CTA/sign-off follows a UI showcase → DO: (a) let the UI breathe (+3-8% in 0.3 s) then contract ease-in to 0.53x with 6px blur/12px smear into (b) localized glitch rectangles (3 rects, 6 frames, sparks #FF4E04 only in one) over a hard cut, (c) logo built from stems (7 frames, blue stem > cyan bloom r 0.06-0.09 > black one stem per 2 frames) with size matched to the contracting UI (0.16 W card to 0.11 W mark at the same centre), (d) never hold the mark (shrink 0.11>0.10 over 0.7 s then 0.07 in 0.16 s), (e) hard cut to the inverted ground and slam the name at 3.5x (1.7 W) with radial streaks (64 copies), 15px cyan/amber fringe, 65px bloom, resolved in ~5 frames (86% of the scale drop in 6 f), then keep creeping 1.0>0.57 over 1.2 s, glow in 3 layers (3/15/45px), ending mid-shrink with 7px zoom blur. BECAUSE the sign-off feels like arriving and leaving at once. (M932)

WHEN type has a weight/scale system → DO keep body at regular (350-500, sentence case, tracking -2.5 to -5% em on display), 6-9% H for statements, 22-33% H for hero figures, 14% H for wordmark (semibold only there), serif for emotional claim lines in the film where UI is sans. BECAUSE bold reads as template; scale contrast replaces weight contrast. (M930-M938)

WHEN holding a still moment → DO never freeze: keep slow shrink (0.82 per 0.6 s), 14°/s dial rotation, slow zoom (0.16 W badge growth over 3 s), a 0.5-0.8 s hold only with something alive (video, dial, drift). Where a true hold exists (M937 2.52-2.60, M931 hover 0.27 s, M938 0.8-1.0 s shape pile) it is pre-wipe. BECAUSE perfectly static frames read as slides. (M932, M936, M937, M931)

WHEN deciding how a clip ends → DO end on an action peak or mid-move (button at 0.81, "weeks" cropped and moving, wordmark mid-shrink, loop curl still visible, final frame hard cut to the next UI) and start the next clip with that momentum; reserve fades for individual objects (line 1 of a headline, 0.75>0.18 over 4 frames). BECAUSE the cut is a beat, not a pause. (M931, M932, M933, M936, M937, M938)

WHEN spending the accent → DO assign one semantic role per colour and spend it on ≤1 element per scene (single word "ideas", single loop, ON-state blue), with the glow colour matching only at events. BECAUSE accent loses power when diffused. (film A/B/C)

rule: WHEN showing a long agent chat or log as proof of volume -> start at frame 0 fully populated and moving. Accelerate continuously from ~6 px/frame to ~250 px/frame (0.35 H/frame) over ~1.8 s. Use no blur, glow or stutter. Let the viewport run EMPTY (2.40) rather than invent filler. Decelerate over ~9 frames onto a short, large, readable list, then hold it still 0.8 s. BECAUSE the viewer reads speed and mass as competence, then gets one legible landing. (M939)

WHEN content passes too fast to read -> make blocks of distinct silhouette (table card, tall red/green diff card, green chips) at 9-14 px text. Keep ONE landmark ~.49 H tall. BECAUSE shapes keep rhythm when words cannot. (M939)

WHEN a new element joins a moving page -> pop it in whole as a step (task_complete card at 2.72, then ride the scroll). Never type, fade or slide it in. BECAUSE a step reads as a system event rather than an animation. (M939, M940)

WHEN wiping between two UI scenes -> use a feathered mask (.31-.42 of frame wide, 0.56-0.6 s) painted in the NEXT scene's ground colour. Start it 0.1-0.2 s before the voice line ends. Start the next hero (a vendor card, 6 px blur) 0.1 s before the wipe completes. Rotate direction across the film: R->L, B->T. BECAUSE overlap kills dead time and the wipe reveals rather than erases. (M939, M940)

WHEN the next scene is empty or one frame of UI -> hard cut (zero frames of fade) and let the new layout arrive already built, then move it (trace panel drops .09 H, decelerating, with the overlay clearing in 0.36 s). BECAUSE a cut with a built layout reads as app state, not as a transition. (M940, M941, M942)

WHEN stacking a list that pushes older items away -> insert the newest at the top as a blank tinted card, fill it 2-4 frames later, shove the stack in piecewise-linear jumps. First jump ~105 px in ONE frame, plus one real 2-frame hold. Add ~.02 W lateral drift per card. Move DOWN if the previous clip scrolled UP. BECAUSE jerky, hold-punctuated steps feel like events being processed. (M940)

WHEN panning a wide timeline -> run every part (sidebar, ruler, blocks) on ONE shared track. Peak ~126 px/frame mid-clip, ~2.9 frame widths total, long tail, no zoom. Fade blocks in at full width, never growing them. Clip with a fixed left gutter. BECAUSE a rigid track reads as camera, and growing bars read as charts. (M940)

WHEN a cursor must "click" -> glide it on an asymptotic curve (~85% of path in the first 0.7 s, then a 0.5 s creep), shrink it 15-20% as it approaches, hold 2 frames still. Press = target compresses ~23% (48 -> 37 px) or arrow to .75 over ~0.24 s, with no ring or flash. Trigger the response on the press-minimum frame. Exit by a fast curved sweep (7 frames, label tilts ~10°). BECAUSE the cause-effect gap of ~0 frames is what sells "real product". (M939, M942, M943)

WHEN expanding a card into a canvas -> animate as a camera zoom-OUT: container grows while its header content shrinks (scale 1 -> .39). Allow one overshoot (.63 -> 1.06 -> .82 of W). Children step in whole every 1-2 frames and are shrunk by the zoom, not by their own tweens. BECAUSE the viewer sees a zoom-out, so the content reads as spatial. (M939)

WHEN a chosen card carries state into a form (the M943 pattern) -> Collapse the card's SURFACE inward around the orb while the children keep size and are cropped by the shrinking rounded mask (10 frames). Shrink the siblings in place and fade them over ~0.16 s. Never slide siblings off. Meanwhile pull focus on the destination form by animating blur 4 -> 0 px over 0.46 s, not opacity. Fly the orb on a curved path: down, left, up, 0.8 s, d .22 W -> .036 W, 5 px blur at peak speed, no overshoot, landing in the form's slot. The destination label changes with the choice (a name -> a name). BECAUSE one continuous object makes the selection a traceable state change. (M942, M943)

WHEN a cursor must cross a scene to commit -> sweep an ARC (dip .23 H below its start, peak 80 px/frame), lean 20° clockwise at peak, one-sided 20-25 px smear, start 0.13 s after the dock lands. Keep it a single persistent arrow. Park it, blurred, in the layer behind between beats. BECAUSE persistence implies a person. (M943, M942)

WHEN switching to a close-up for a button press -> use ONE 50% double-exposed frame, then the 2.33x layout as a hard state. Scale the cursor less (1.5x). Glide in slowly for ~1 s. Press: 12% cursor shrink and 0.97 button scale for 0.1 s. Anticipate with a violet shadow growing to ~22 px. Burst 5 frames, width x2.2, blur 3 -> 25 px. Cut mid-burst. BECAUSE the viewer fills in the rest. (M943)

WHEN a product window arrives -> open from a slit (.10 W) with top and bottom edges fixed, content cropped and never stretched. Pause growth, then jump +.22 W in ONE frame. Slide panel and gallery up on two slightly different tracks (16 px smear at peak). Reveal sidebar rows top-down as the clip edge passes. Dock the logo disc to the sidebar slot concurrently (.10 -> .04 W, 20 px smear at peak). Reach rest by 1.4 s. BECAUSE the UI is staged (clip + rise) before it is read. (M944)

WHEN the hero beat is done and titles must take over -> tip the window back (y .11 -> .46, sides splay, lower half off-frame, 1.1 s), then drift only ~4 px for 2.3 s. Release the disc on an up-right arc (slow until 2.93, 65 px/frame peak at 3.03). Titles rise .06 H while alpha ramps linearly over 0.83 s; subtitle words stagger 3 frames. BECAUSE the foreground becomes a plinth and the headline gets clean space. (M944)

WHEN changing light/state colours -> use hard plateaus of 0.3-0.4 s with a 1-frame gap. Sync disc core, halo and window rim. Order white, teal, cyan, white. Never cross-fade. BECAUSE a hard step reads as a mode change. (M944)

WHEN ending a film on motion without a card -> accelerate a roll to -76° with smear on the UI (22/18 px) and sharp-ish titles (2 px, -20%). Never settle. BECAUSE the next shot takes over the momentum. (M944)

WHEN revealing a big number -> resolve it left to right from pixel squares and ASCII glyphs (final value from the first frame, a leading band 12-15 px). Scale it 96 -> 176 px while it resolves. Reach crisp in 0.7 s, hold ~0.47 s (it is one number), dissolve from both ends toward the centre in 0.33 s. Move the label plate DOWN, not up. BECAUSE it shows magnitude without a counter ticking. (M945)

WHEN gathering integrations around a product mark -> 9 upright tiles at 40° spacing, clockwise. Run the radius collapse fast (.63 -> .29 H in 8 frames) while the swirl decelerates 17 -> 10 -> 1°/frame. Bloat each tile 1.8x for ~4 frames in a wave that travels AGAINST the orbit, widening gaps 0.07 -> 0.27 s. Build the badge inside the orbit (disc .46 scale fading in, flame filling bottom-up from squares). Exit the tiles in a clockwise stagger (2-3 frames) with accelerating orbit. BECAUSE counter-rotation and the wave keep identity while the badge builds. (M945)

WHEN swapping an integration (carousel) -> move both candidates together (spacing .49 H), in steps with real holds: jump 0.12 H in 1 frame, hold 2, decelerate, hold 1. Keep the outgoing disc fading and shrinking (.9 -> .7x) while the incoming one scales .7 -> 1.0 and darkens 18% -> black. Break and re-link the connector by tint and bracket shape only (gray -> rust -> orange #CB4200, no glow or scale), and change it in ONE frame after the column rests (4.87 in M945). BECAUSE the link is the only thing that must feel "alive". (M945, M946)

WHEN closing on a logo -> make the preceding wipe a motif from the scene (the horn's white wave, stair-notched) and jerk the world left with accelerating offsets (-.04, -.10, -.29, -.41, -.63, -.86) with one repeated frame. Resolve the flame inside its silhouette (dots, then solid rising from the base, 0.6 s) and the word left to right with a solid front (~13 frames, paired frames). Let both drift ~.09 W left while resolving. Hold it 3.66 s with the flame tip swaying ±1% W (irregular ~1 s) and a static wordmark. End on the hold, no fade. BECAUSE the brand is "built" from the scene's own texture and the sway keeps a long hold alive. (M946)

WHEN a rolodex/stack opens a brand hook -> mirror two perspective stacks about the logo (outer sheets wider, top photos inverted), start them already on screen. Flip fast (0.1 s), advance slow (1.5 s), then spin clockwise as one rigid unit with rotation 2 -> 4 -> 11 -> 29 -> 74° and scale 1 -> 2.0 over 0.7 s with 10 px blur. Cut on frame while still big. BECAUSE the logo reads as the fixed centre that the whole moving machine revolves around. (M941)

WHEN a ring of photo cards orbits a headline -> use 10 upright cards of IRREGULAR size, tall ones further out. Enter by ease-out convergence (smear halves every ~0.15 s), then decelerate continuously (217 -> 75°/s), then fling outward 7x speed while the headline swells 1 -> 1.3. Let cards overlap the headline text and stay constant in size. Place the headline at vertical centre with word staggers of 5 frames. BECAUSE irregularity and overlap look photographed and not generated. (M941)

WHEN lighting a headline word by word -> each word starts .07 H low and grey (#B8B8B8, 1.5 px blur), rises over 0.67 s and goes black over 0.33 s. 5-frame stagger. BECAUSE reading order is locked and no word pops. (M941, M944)
WHEN typing a prompt in a demo -> reveal discrete prefixes at ~1 grapheme per frame with occasional 1-frame holds. No caret. About 1 s for 40 characters. BECAUSE it looks keyed, not animated. (M942)

WHEN defocusing background UI behind a hero -> blur it to ~4 px (copy still readable), hold, let the cursor blur with it, and never fade to grey. BECAUSE depth is carried by blur and readable copy stays on-screen. (M942, M943)

WHEN a spoken question or claim opens the piece -> DO put one word at a time on a near-empty page, 1-2 pose gaps apart (M947: 2,2,4,4 frames at 60 fps; M958: 0.27/0.16/0.17 s; M956: 0.06-0.10 s), each arriving oversized or offset and landing with strong ease-out, and RE-CENTRE the line each time (M947) or lay out final slots first and never re-centre (M956) -> BECAUSE arrival rhythm reads as speech, and the line is visibly still being formed. (M947, M956, M958)

WHEN a word is the first thing on screen -> DO start it 4-5x oversize and blurred (M947 "Ready" 0.39H -> 0.09H in 0.30 s; M953 red words 1.44x) so ~85% of the shrink happens in the first 8 frames and a 0.3-0.5 s tail finishes it -> BECAUSE it lands like a hit but does not bounce. Never overshoot. (M947, M953, M959)
